sections.html:
Across the Connecticut River from the city of Hartford, East Hartford holds the east bank in Hartford County. The town sits in the Capitol Planning Region and measures 18.7 square miles, 0.73 of which is water. Burnside, Hockanum and Mayberry Village are among its neighborhoods, and 51,045 people lived here at the 2020 census.

Elevation is only about 49 feet, close to the river, which makes drainage and basement moisture worth checking before you sell. The town was incorporated in October 1783 and has run under a Town Council charter since 1929.

Farming, with tobacco the main crop, dominated East Hartford until 1929, when Pratt & Whitney moved production here from Hartford onto a site of about 1,100 acres. Population went from 17,125 in 1930 to 57,583 in 1970, slid to about 50,000 by 1990 and has hovered near 51,000 since 2010.

Most of that growth came in the forty years after 1930, so the housing leans toward mid-century construction. Farmland gave way to streets of houses over those decades, and sellers see the age in what buyers ask about. Buyers will want to hear how old the roof, wiring and heating system are.

Expect cold winters and warm, humid summers. January averages 27.9 degrees, July 74.5 with an average daily high of 84.2, and annual precipitation is about 50.22 inches. October, December, June and August are the wettest months, at roughly 4.6 to 4.8 inches each.

Rain in every month keeps roofs, gutters and foundation drainage busy. In a traditional sale, an inspector will mark down a deferred roof or a wet basement.

sections.h2: A large employer and local demand
sections.html:
Pratt & Whitney, the aerospace engine maker, is headquartered at 400 Main Street and occupies a large share of the town's land. Its plant once employed tens of thousands, and local demand still tends to follow its hiring.

That is worth asking a local professional about if you are pricing a house in your part of town, since a recent change at the plant can shift who is buying.

Once an offer is accepted, the title company or attorney orders a title search, confirms the payoffs and prepares the deed. Meanwhile you book final utility readings and clear the house. If a buyer wants a walkthrough, it usually happens in this window. On closing day the deed is signed, the conveyance tax return is filed with the recording, and the payoffs are paid first. Whatever remains is released to you.

Little of that changes whether the sale is a listing or a direct cash sale. What changes is the number of steps that come before it, and how many of them can fall through.

Each of these shows up on a final bill at closing, so knowing the providers lets you schedule final readings.

  • Electricity: Eversource Energy
  • Water: the Metropolitan District Commission
  • Natural gas: Connecticut Natural Gas
  • Phone and fiber internet: Frontier Communications
  • Cable television and internet: Comcast

A water or sewer balance left unpaid can follow the property, so request final readings and clear anything open before the closing date.

The 2025 Grand List bills were paid in installments, and the first came due July 1 with a grace period into August. For the second installment date and the current mill rate, call the tax office. The collector takes online payments, mail and the drop box outside Town Hall, and honors USPS postmarks outside business hours.

Tax office detailHow to reach it
Tax collector phone(860) 291-7257
Tax office emailTax@easthartfordct.gov
Accounts coded TaxServ (delinquent)Pay TaxServ directly, (860) 724-9100

Delinquent motor vehicle or personal property tax can go to a state marshal under a warrant. The collector explains that process on its website.

sections.h2: State conveyance tax when you sell
sections.html:
Connecticut's conveyance tax return is the seller's job, or the seller's lawyer's, and it goes in as the deed is recorded. East Hartford shows as town code 043, and any price from $2,000 up is taxed unless the transfer is exempt.

Exemptions that come up most for house sales:

  • Transfers between spouses.
  • Handing over a principal residence by deed in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Selling a principal residence for less than its mortgages plus priority tax or sewer liens.
  • A principal residence with a pyrrhotite crumbling foundation, once a professional engineer has evaluated it in writing.

The exemption code goes on the return, and your closing attorney can say whether one fits.

sections.h2: Seller checklist before choosing a route
sections.html:
Paperwork and property both set the timeline, so a quick checklist keeps surprises out of closing week.

  • Confirm your tax balance at (860) 291-7257 or Tax@easthartfordct.gov.
  • Ask the assessor how your property is classified and what it is assessed at.
  • Gather leases, permits and repair records.
  • Write down the utility account names for final readings.
  • List liens, judgments or a mortgage balance that closing must clear.

If the house came through an estate, add the probate papers. A title company needs to see who can sign the deed.

Back taxes slow a sale, but they do not stop one. Start by calling the tax office to learn which account the balance sits on. Most accounts are with the collector, but some delinquent ones are coded TaxServ and are paid there directly. Get the payoff on paper, with the date it stays valid.

The closing agent then pays the balance, plus any lien or open water and sewer charge, out of your proceeds before you are paid. Delinquent motor vehicle or personal property tax is separate and can reach a state marshal, so ask whether anything like that is under your name before the deed is signed.

A cash buyer is generally comfortable taking on a house with a tax backlog, because the offer is built around the payoff. A buyer relying on a mortgage may find the lien harder to work through, and the lender will want it cleared before funding. Ask the title company early which payoffs it expects to see.

sections.h2: A cash sale in East Hartford
sections.html:
Mid-century houses needing updates, multi-unit properties, inherited houses and mortgages in arrears are common here, and a cash sale avoids the repair and showing steps.

  1. Share the address, how the house looks and when you need to be out.
  2. We study the facts and offer on the house as it is.
  3. When you agree, a title company or attorney drafts the deed and files the state return.
  4. At closing, liens and back taxes come out of the proceeds.

We set no price before reviewing the property. Measure any offer against a listing, then decide.

faqs.q: When are East Hartford property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first installment on the 2025 Grand List was due July 1, with a grace period into August. Ask the tax collector, (860) 291-7257, for the second installment date.

faqs.q: Who provides electricity and water in East Hartford?
faqs.a: Eversource supplies electricity and the Metropolitan District Commission supplies water. Connecticut Natural Gas provides gas.

faqs.q: Does East Hartford have a state conveyance tax when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. You file the return as the deed is recorded, and a price of $2,000 or more is taxed unless an exemption fits. Your closing attorney can calculate it.

faqs.q: Can I sell an East Hartford house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers purchase as is, with no repairs or cleanup beforehand.

faqs.q: What if my East Hartford taxes are overdue?
faqs.a: At closing, overdue taxes come out of your proceeds. Some delinquent accounts sit with TaxServ, and the tax office can confirm your balance.
